data.long_meaning: Hima is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘himā’ meaning frost or snow. In Hindu mythology, Hima is the name of a celestial nymph, the goddess of snow. She is the wife of the sage Kashyapa, and the mother of many legendary kings and heroes. The name Hima carries the meaning “Frost, Snow” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Hima usually hope their child will grow to embody frost, snow and live with faith, good character and purpose.

She is believed to bless her devotees with prosperity, good fortune, fertility, wealth and happiness. The name is also popular in India, where it continues to be given to baby girls.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Hima is deeply spiritual and symbolizes purity, coolness, and tranquility. It reflects the inner peace and calmness of the soul. The goddess Hima is also associated with the cremation ground, symbolizing transformation and rebirth. This spiritual connection to the cycle of life and death invites introspection and reflection, encouraging one to live with awareness and mindfulness.
